issues.title: Length-aware selectivity for substring contains() scan filters
issues.hypothesis: In q09 the scan filter on part is `contains(p_name,'<word>')` (LIKE '%x%' rewritten), stored as an ExpressionFilter. RelationStatisticsHelper::InspectTableFilter (relation_statistics_helper.cpp:446) ignores EXPRESSION_FILTER, so ExtractGetStats falls back to DEFAULT_SELECTIVITY=0.2: part est 400K (actual 109K, 5.4%), so lineitem⋈part is estimated at 12M when it is 3.27M. Because of this the probe pipeline ends up probing two large build sides: orders (15M rows, HASH_JOIN 2.9s CPU) and partsupp⋈supplier⋈nation (8M rows, HASH_JOIN 2.65s CPU). These are the two biggest operators after the lineitem scan (5.0s). Building a 15M/8M-row HT is mostly random memory writes. I forced the flipped plans (disabled_optimizers='join_order,build_side_probe_side' with an explicit join tree) so that lineitem⋈part (3.27M) is the build side and orders/partsupp are probed. Measured operator CPU: orders HJ 2.9s -> 2.0-2.2s, ps HJ 2.65s -> 1.67s. That is before any BF reaches those probe scans; see the other two issues. BuildProbeSideOptimizer::GetBuildSize/TryFlipJoinChildren needs the left estimate below about 10M rows to flip the orders join (narrow 2-col right side, 1.15 right-deep penalty), and below about 4.8M rows to flip the 8M partsupp join (the left side is wider). So the part selectivity estimate has to drop to about 0.06-0.08.
issues.plan: In src/optimizer/join_order/relation_statistics_helper.cpp InspectTableFilter, add `case TableFilterType::EXPRESSION_FILTER`: cast to ExpressionFilter. If `expr` is a BoundFunctionExpression whose function name is `contains` (also accept `like`/`~~` patterns that are '%lit%' with no other wildcards, if they survive to here), with child[0] a column ref (or BoundReferenceExpression) and child[1] a non-NULL VARCHAR BoundConstantExpression with literal length L>=1, return cardinality * clamp(0.2 * 0.75^L, 0.01, 0.2), rounded up, minimum 1. Do NOT match NOT(...) or OR expressions; anything else keeps returning the input cardinality, so the existing default-0.2 path is unchanged. Because ExtractGetStats treats any reduction as 'has_equality_filter', the 0.2 fallback is then skipped for this table. Also check the CONJUNCTION_AND path, since contains may be ANDed with other filters on the same column. Check EXPLAIN on all 4 q09 instances (dark/deep/ghost/aquamarine, L=4..10): lineitem⋈part should become the build side of both the orders join and the partsupp join. Report which flips happened. Then run bench.
issues.expected_gain: q09: -8..-15% (orders and ps joins together save about 1.5-2s CPU of about 14s in forced-plan tests). It is also the enabler for the BF-on-flipped-probe issues, which could bring q09 to about -30%.
issues.generality: Any query with a positive substring predicate (LIKE '%x%', contains) on a dimension table that is joined to a fact table. Today such filters are all estimated at a flat 20%, which hides how selective they are. Longer literals are more selective, the same principle PostgreSQL's like selectivity uses. Plans can change for hidden templates that have positive contains filters. NOT LIKE (q13/q16 style) is excluded and unchanged.
issues.risk: Medium-low. It is estimation only, so correctness is unaffected. A plan regression is possible if the true selectivity of a long literal is much higher than estimated (for example a common word). The 0.01 floor limits how far the estimate can drop.

issues.title: Push join filters through compressed-materialization compress projections
issues.hypothesis: Join filter pushdown runs after compressed materialization (optimizer.cpp: STATISTICS_PROPAGATION at line 289 inserts __internal_compress_integral_* projections; JOIN_FILTER_PUSHDOWN is at line 320). PushdownJoinFilterExpression (join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp:23) only passes column refs and integral casts, so a probe chain scan -> PROJECTION(__internal_compress_integral_uinteger(key, min)) -> join gets no dynamic filters at all. I observed this in the forced flipped q09 plan: the orders scan (15M rows) and the partsupp scan (8M) had no min/max and no BF, while the lineitem side did. Once the probe/build flip happens (contains-selectivity issue), BF on o_orderkey from 3.27M build keys would cut the orders probe from 15M rows to about 3.3M.
issues.plan: In PushdownJoinFilterExpression, handle BOUND_FUNCTION whose function is one of the CM integral compress functions (__internal_compress_integral_*; see src/function/scalar/compressed_materialization/ and compressed_materialization_utils.hpp). Child 0 is the column, child 1 is the constant min offset. Record the offset in JoinFilterPushdownColumn (new field). In JoinFilterPushdownInfo::FinalizeFilters (physical_hash_join.cpp:814), add the offset back to min/max before casting to the storage type. For BF: hashes are taken on the join-key values (compressed), so the BF cannot be used unless the build key is uncompressed in the same way. Simplest correct rule: allow the BF only when probe and build condition types match after decompression; otherwise push min/max only. Check how the build side key is compressed for this join first.
issues.expected_gain: q09: 0% on the current plan. After the flip it could be -10% or more (orders join 2s CPU -> ~0.5s).
issues.generality: Any hash join whose probe side scan key is compressed by CM before the join, which is common for integer FK keys with known ranges.
issues.risk: Medium: offset arithmetic and type casts in filter values. A wrong offset gives wrong results, so it needs tests with non-zero min.

issues.title: Bloom filter on one key of multi-condition equality hash joins
issues.hypothesis: CanUseBloomFilter (physical_hash_join.cpp:775) requires ht->conditions.size()==1, so joins on (partkey, suppkey) never get a BF. After the flip, the partsupp probe (8M rows) joins on 2 keys against 3.27M build rows that hold only about 436K distinct partkeys. A BF on ps_partkey alone would drop about 95% of probe rows (forced plan: ps HJ 1.67s CPU while probing all 8M rows).
issues.plan: Allow building a BF on a single equality condition column of a multi-condition join: hash only that column's build values during HT build, in a separate hash vector, and push BFTableFilter for that probe column. Choose the condition column with the highest estimated selectivity, or simply the first COMPARE_EQUAL condition. Requires JoinHashTable to compute the per-column hash (join_hashtable.cpp:720 InsertHashes currently uses the combined hash).
issues.expected_gain: q09: ~-8% after the flip (ps HJ 1.67s -> ~0.3s CPU)
issues.generality: Any multi-key equi-join with a selective build side, for example composite-FK joins.
issues.risk: Medium: extra hash per build row; the BF must be keyed on the single-column hash.
